issues.t: Lower intake manifold gasket leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping with no puddle you can find, a sweet smell after driving, the temperature gauge creeping up, or milky, light-brown oil on the dipstick.
issues.why: The original plastic-framed lower intake gaskets on the 3800 V6 break down with age and coolant. Coolant can then leak outside the engine or seep into the oil, which wears the bearings.
issues.next: Check the coolant and oil regularly. If the oil looks milky, stop driving and have it fixed right away, because coolant in the oil can ruin the engine. Ask for the updated steel-core gaskets and a coolant flush.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips or loses forward gears
issues.sym: The engine revs but the car is slow to pick up speed, gears slip or flare between shifts, or the car will barely move forward.
issues.why: The 4T65E automatic in these cars is known for worn clutches, a burnt fourth-gear clutch and a failing input gear thrust bearing, usually after high mileage or overheated fluid.
issues.next: Have the fluid level and condition checked and the codes read as soon as slipping starts. Catching it early can sometimes mean a valve body or solenoid repair instead of a full rebuild.

issues.t: Long, harsh shifts with code P1811 or P0748
issues.sym: Firm or banging upshifts, shifts that seem to take a long time, and a check engine light with codes such as P1811 or P0748.
issues.why: The transmission pressure control solenoid and valve body wear, so line pressure is not controlled well and the computer flags slow shifts.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid checked. A pressure control solenoid, valve body repair or shift-correction kit is often enough if it is handled before the clutches burn up.

issues.t: Harsh clunk into reverse or drive
issues.sym: A hard bump or clunk when shifting from Park into Reverse or Drive, often worse when the car is cold.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for harsh engagement on these transmissions, tied to valve body and control issues rather than a broken part.
issues.next: Mention the clunk to a shop and ask them to check the transmission bulletins and the engine and transmission mounts.

issues.t: Transmission cooler lines rust and leak
issues.sym: Red fluid dripping near the front of the car or under the radiator, and shifting problems if the level gets low.
issues.why: The steel cooler lines and their fittings rust through in salted winter climates.
issues.next: Have the lines inspected if you see red fluid. Replace the rusted section before the fluid runs low and damages the transmission.

issues.t: Plastic coolant elbows and upper intake leak
issues.sym: A coolant smell, wet residue on top of the engine near the throttle body, or a slowly dropping coolant level.
issues.why: The plastic coolant elbows on the 3800 V6, and the plastic upper intake on the non-supercharged engine, crack or leak at their gaskets as they age.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure tested to find the leak. These are small parts, but running the engine low on coolant can cause overheating.

issues.t: Misfire from corroded fuel injector connections
issues.sym: Rough running, a shaking idle, hesitation, and a flashing or steady check engine light, often worse in damp weather.
issues.why: GM found that the fuel injector electrical connectors can wear and corrode where they touch, which cuts the signal to the injector.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. A shop can clean or replace the injector connectors following the GM bulletin before replacing injectors.

issues.t: Hard starts and rough idle from clogged fuel injectors
issues.sym: Long cranking before the engine starts, chugging, a rough idle or a misfire, especially on a cold engine.
issues.why: Deposits build up in the fuel injectors over time, so they spray poorly. GM issued a bulletin for this on the 3800 V6.
issues.next: Ask for a fuel system cleaning or injector service first. If one injector is badly clogged, it may need to be replaced.

issues.t: Engine stalls from a failing crankshaft or airflow sensor
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving or at a stop, then may restart after it cools down. The check engine light may or may not come on.
issues.why: A failing crankshaft position sensor or mass airflow sensor sends a bad signal to the engine computer, which can shut the engine off.
issues.next: Stalling is a safety risk, so get it checked soon. Have stored codes read; the crank sensor is a common fix.

issues.t: Misfire from a failing ignition coil
issues.sym: A stumble or shake while cruising or accelerating, a flashing check engine light, and codes for a single cylinder or a pair of cylinders.
issues.why: The 3800 uses coil packs that each fire two cylinders. A coil or its corroded tower can fail with age.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. Replacing the bad coil and checking the spark plug wires usually fixes it.

issues.t: Oil leak from oil pan gasket or rear main seal
issues.sym: Oil spots under the middle of the car and a low oil level between changes.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for repeat oil pan gasket leaks and rear main seal leaks on the 3800 V6.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up and have the source found. An oil pan gasket is a moderate job; a rear main seal is a bigger job because the transmission must come out.

issues.t: Valve cover gasket oil leak
issues.sym: A burning oil smell after driving, light smoke from the engine bay, or oily residue around the valve covers.
issues.why: The valve cover gaskets harden with age and let oil seep onto the hot exhaust manifolds.
issues.next: Replace the gaskets when you notice the smell. Oil dripping on a hot exhaust is a fire risk if left for a long time.

issues.t: Rear air shocks or leveling compressor fail
issues.sym: The rear of the car sits low, bounces over bumps, or the leveling compressor runs a lot or not at all.
issues.why: Many Park Avenues have rear air shocks with an automatic leveling compressor. The rubber air shocks leak and the compressor wears out.
issues.next: Have the rear shocks and air lines checked. Some owners replace the system with conventional shocks.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing hums or has play
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that rises with speed, looseness in the front end, and sometimes an ABS light.
issues.why: The sealed front hub and bearing assemblies wear out, and the ABS wheel speed sensor is built into the hub.
issues.next: Have the hubs checked for play and noise. Replace the worn hub; a badly worn bearing can affect steering and braking.

issues.t: Worn front struts and suspension parts
issues.sym: A bouncy or loose ride, clunks over bumps, and uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Front struts, strut mounts and tie rods wear out with mileage on these heavy cars. GM also issued bulletins for squeaks from the front struts.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected and aligned. Replace worn struts and tie rods in pairs.

issues.t: Clunk or rattle from the steering column
issues.sym: A clunk or rattle felt through the steering wheel over bumps or when turning at low speed.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for noise from the lower steering column shaft and bearing on these years.
issues.next: Have the steering inspected to rule out worn tie rods, then ask about the GM steering column bulletin.

issues.t: Power steering moan or squawk at low speed
issues.sym: A moan, groan or squawk when turning the wheel in parking lots or at low speed.
issues.why: GM issued several bulletins for steering gear and power steering moan on these cars, often tied to the fluid or the steering gear valve.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level and look for leaks. A shop can follow the GM bulletin before replacing major parts.

issues.t: Shake or vibration at highway speed
issues.sym: A shake in the steering wheel or seat at highway speeds.
issues.why: GM issued several updated bulletins for highway shake, often fixed by road-force tire balancing or replacing out-of-round tires or wheels.
issues.next: Ask the tire shop for a road-force balance. If the shake stays, have the wheel bearings and front end checked.

issues.t: ABS or traction light from a wheel speed sensor
issues.sym: The ABS or traction control light comes on and stays on, sometimes with a stability message.
issues.why: A wheel speed sensor or its wiring fails, often the one built into a front hub, and the ABS system shuts itself off.
issues.next: The normal brakes still work, but ABS does not. Have the codes read to find which wheel sensor or hub is at fault.

issues.t: Heater and A/C blend door actuators fail
issues.sym: Air comes out of the wrong vents, the temperature will not change, or you hear clicking behind the dash.
issues.why: The small electric motors that move the air mode and temperature doors inside the dash wear out.
issues.next: Have the climate system tested. Replacing the failed actuator is usually all that is needed.

issues.t: Leaking fuel pressure regulator can cause a backfire and fire (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel smell, hard starting, or a loud backfire through the intake.
issues.why: Some fuel pressure regulators on the non-supercharged 3800 V6 leak, which can cause a backfire that cracks the intake and lets fuel leak.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check with a Buick dealer using your VIN to confirm the regulator recall was done. Do not ignore a fuel smell.

issues.t: Anti-lock brake defect can lengthen stopping (recall)
issues.sym: The car may take longer than normal to stop.
issues.why: A defect in the anti-lock brake system on some 1997 cars could increase stopping distance.
issues.next: Have a Buick dealer check your VIN to confirm the recall repair was done.

issues.t: Seat belt system may not hold in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The problem only shows up in a crash.
issues.why: On some 1997 cars, the seat belt anchorages might not handle the required load in a crash.
issues.next: Have a Buick dealer check your VIN to make sure the recall repair was done.

issues.t: Shoulder belt can jam in the retractor (recall)
issues.sym: The shoulder belt will not pull out or locks up and cannot be used.
issues.why: The belt webbing can get jammed inside the retractor.
issues.next: Do not let anyone ride in a seat with a jammed belt. Have a dealer check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Loose brake booster nuts can affect braking (recall)
issues.sym: A brake pedal that sits lower than normal, brakes that drag, or fumes or water entering the cabin.
issues.why: On some 1999 cars, the nuts holding the brake booster and pedal assembly can loosen.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Have a Buick dealer check your VIN. If your pedal feels different, get it inspected before driving further.

issues.t: Car can pull to one side when braking (recall)
issues.sym: The car pulls left or right when you brake, and stops take longer.
issues.why: A small number of 1999 cars had a brake defect that could cause pulling under braking.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN for the recall and inspect the brakes.

issues.t: ABS unit can leak internally (recall)
issues.sym: The ABS light may come on and the brake pedal may feel different.
issues.why: Some anti-lock brake hydraulic units can leak fluid internally.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN. They will inspect the ABS unit and replace it if needed.

issues.t: Windshield wipers can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers quit in low or high speed, often after the electrical system has a voltage spike.
issues.why: The chip inside the wiper motor control can lock up after voltage changes.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN for the wiper recall. Do not drive in rain or snow without working wipers.

issues.t: Emergency trunk release can be hard to pull (recall)
issues.sym: The glow-in-the-dark release handle inside the trunk needs a lot of force or does not open the lid.
issues.why: The release cable can be out of position, which raises the force needed to open the latch from inside.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN for the recall. Teach children that the trunk is not a play area.
